question: True or false: colour films from the 1940s often survive in truer colour than films from the 1970s?
answer: True. Three-strip Technicolor recorded each scene on three black-and-white negatives, one per primary colour, and silver images barely fade. From the 1950s most films used single-strip Eastmancolor, whose dyes decay; many 1970s prints and negatives have faded towards pink. A 1939 film can be reprinted from its separations with its colour intact.
move: Newer is not sturdier; ask what the thing is made of.
trap: Assuming newer film stock must have kept its colour better.
source: Read and Meyer, Restoration of Motion Picture Film
reference: Read and Meyer, Restoration of Motion Picture Film, Butterworth-Heinemann, 2000
